# manual capture: what FORM the failure takes, over repeated runs, on four builds
# harness:  crash-form.py   (re-runnable: `python crash-form.py [dxc.exe] [runs]`)
# repro:    repro.hlsl with the arguments in cmd.txt (-T ps_6_0 -E main_fragment)
# NOTE:     hand-driven capture, not a probe. Not scored by match.json.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS
# The failing code is an out-of-bounds std::vector index --
#   lib/Transforms/Scalar/ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:4791  DXASSERT(argIdx < endArgIdx, ...)
#   lib/Transforms/Scalar/ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:4792  FlatAnnotationList[argIdx]
# and NDEBUG turns that DXASSERT into `do { } while (0)` (include/dxc/Support/Global.h:356),
# so every release binary runs the unguarded index. What happens next depends on the heap
# bytes that follow the vector, so the exit status AND the message vary -- between releases,
# and on some builds between runs of the SAME binary.
#
# This is the evidence for why match.json is `internal_failure` (exit-status based) rather
# than a text match: 8 of the 20 release binaries fail with completely empty stderr, and a
# text predicate would have scored those 8 clean and invented a fix boundary that does not
# exist. Every one of the 40 runs below is an internal failure; not one produced DXIL, and
# not one produced a diagnostic.
#
# ran: 2026-08-07 (see per-block output)
